name: cat-catch-and-avoid
title: Catch Circles, Avoid Diamonds
question:
Does the evolved agent catch falling circles and avoid falling diamonds from
the committed seeded genome, across the trained range of object offsets?
hypothesis:
The agent ends close to circles (within the catch radius) and far from diamonds
at every trained offset (−6..+6), a clean behavioural categorization.
objective:
Replay the committed seed over the five training offsets × two shapes and
measure the final horizontal distance to the object for each.
claim:
The agent catches circles (mean final distance 0.15, caught at all offsets) and
avoids diamonds (mean final distance 29.6) — a category gap > 8.
description:
The seeded CTRNN agent (5 neurons, 7 ray sensors, 2 motors) is decoded from
data/genomes/categorical_perception.npz and run deterministically. The
behaviour is pinned by tests/test_categorical_seed.py.

expected_behavior.name: catches-circles-avoids-diamonds
expected_behavior.condition: committed seed, offsets −6..+6, objects size 3, 200 steps @ dt=0.1
expected_behavior.rationale:
Circles: mean final distance < 1.5 (caught at every offset). Diamonds: mean
final distance > 10, with circle→diamond separation > 8. Verified in the
suite (test_seed_catches_circles_and_avoids_diamonds,
test_seed_catches_every_circle_offset).

findings.summary: Clean catch/avoid: circle mean fd 0.15 (all caught), diamond mean fd 29.6.
findings.detail:
figures/trajectories.png shows the agent converging onto each circle's
position and fleeing each diamond. The early trajectory is shared across
shapes (active perception) before the system commits.
